Deployment and Integration Guide

Updated: 2026-09-21

← Back to documents

Introduces onboard, shore-side, and hybrid deployment scenarios, runtime environment requirements, and integration flows using NMEA and WebSocket interfaces.

DeploymentIntegration

The deployment model depends on the scenario: a single vessel values offline availability, fleet management values centralized data, and ship-to-shore collaboration requires both ends to exchange data. The three models can be combined.

Deployment models

ModelScenarioNotes
Onboard deploymentSingle-vessel navigation supportRuns locally offline, with chart data and permits updated aboard
Shore-side deploymentFleet and dispatch managementCentralized management of chart and voyage data for unified maintenance
Hybrid deploymentShip-to-shore collaborationOnboard system works offline and synchronizes with shore after berthing

Runtime environment

  • Operating system: Windows and Linux environments are supported, with domestic platform adaptation assessed per project.
  • Hardware: sized by chart data volume and concurrent track count; the exact baseline follows the project technical proposal.
  • Network: offline operation is supported, and chart data plus permits can be imported from offline media.

Interface integration

  • Position and attitude input: common formats such as NMEA 0183 and NMEA 2000.
  • Warning and status output: warning events and voyage status can be published over WebSocket or HTTP.
  • Integration support: interface notes, field lists, and joint debugging examples are available.

Implementation flow

  1. Requirement confirmation: agree on vessel type, waters, data format, and warning scope.
  2. Environment preparation: confirm operating system, hardware, and network conditions.
  3. Data import: load chart data and permit files and verify coverage.
  4. Interface joint debugging: validate position input and warning event output.
  5. Trial run and delivery: adjust configuration based on the trial run, then deliver.
Specific environment baselines and interface details follow the project technical proposal agreed by both parties.
